messages:
ryan: Hey team — since we migrated my-app to the new VPC (NAT gateway) we see intermittent failures when calling our private KMS -> HSM. Errors are 502 / TLS timeouts. Started after the cutover at ~10:20 UTC. Can you help triage?

maria: Can you paste the app-side error and any agent logs you have? Also whether this affects all regions or just one.

ryan: App log snippets:
```
2026-02-22T10:25:12Z error: downstream call to KMS failed: tls handshake error: unexpected message
2026-02-22T10:25:12Z warn: retrying key fetch, attempt=2
2026-02-22T10:25:15Z error: dial tcp 10.11.12.13:443: i/o timeout
```
HSM is behind a vendor-managed appliance at 10.11.12.13 (peered via our provider). Only affects keys stored on that HSM; other KMS-backed keys OK.

maria: Do you see any DNS failures (NXDOMAIN / SERVFAIL) or is it pure TCP/TLS? Also can you run a quick tcpdump on the app host capturing the failing flow?

ryan: tcpdump from the app host during a failure (filtered):
```
12:03:05.123456 IP app-eni > 10.11.12.13: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0], length 0
12:03:05.123789 IP 10.11.12.13 > app-eni: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 29200, options [mss 1400], length 0
12:03:05.124000 IP app-eni > 10.11.12.13: Flags [P.], seq 1:241, ack 1, win 229, length 240
12:03:05.124150 IP (frag 1/2) app-eni > 10.11.12.13: frag 0, id 54321, offset 0
12:03:05.124300 IP (frag 2/2) app-eni > 10.11.12.13: frag 1, id 54321, offset 1480
12:03:05.124800 IP 10.11.12.13 > app-eni: ICMP frag-needed, mtu 1400
```
So we see fragmentation and an ICMP "fragmentation needed". The NAT gateway sets DF so fragments are being dropped somewhere.

kevin: This looks like a classic PMTU/MSS issue with the NAT gateway or a transit device. TLS records get split across fragments; some HSM appliances or middleboxes drop or mishandle fragments causing handshake failures. Two quick tests: 1) lower MTU/MSS on the app ENI to 1400 or 2) enable MSS clamping on the NAT/gateway path. Also ensure ICMP "fragmentation needed" is allowed back to the host so PMTU discovery completes.

maria: Can you try the MSS-clamp iptables rule on a test host and retest? Example to clamp MSS for outbound TCP: 
```
sudo iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```
If that fixes it, we can push as a short-term mitigation while we update the NAT gateway config.

ryan: Applied MSS clamp on one replica and failures stopped immediately. curl to the HSM now succeeds:
```
curl -v https://10.11.12.13/health --resolve 10.11.12.13:443:10.11.12.13
* Connected to 10.11.12.13 (10.11.12.13) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: 10.11.12.13

< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

kevin: Good. Longer-term we should: 1) add MSS clamping at the NAT gateway (or enable TCP MSS adjust / PMTU-aware routing), 2) allow ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed) through egress allowlists/firewalls so PMTU discovery works, 3) verify HSM appliance doesn't drop fragments (vendor config), and 4) update runbook for private deployments to include MTU checks.

sarah: Also note that some firewall appliances block ICMP silently; please ensure the customer-facing egress allowlist includes return ICMP for PMTU. For DNS: if DNS lookups to the vendor resolver were timing out earlier, that was likely unrelated but double-check that ephemeral source ports are allowed for UDP/53 responses.

maria: Action items:
- ry an: schedule a 30m maintenance window to apply NAT/GW MSS clamp and update monitoring (owner: ryan)
- kevin: coordinate with cloud infra to add NAT-level MSS clamp and confirm packet capture post-change (owner: kevin)
- sarah: update support runbook with MTU/MSS troubleshooting steps and ICMP allowlist note (owner: sarah)
- ops-bot: create incident ticket and attach tcpdump/logs

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0412. Attach logs at https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-0412

ryan: Will do the maintenance tonight at 02:00 UTC and report back. Thanks all — MSS clamp is a good workaround until NAT config is changed.

maria: Thanks — once you confirm post-change please paste tcpdump + curl output and we'll close the escalation. If vendor HSM still drops fragments we may need a dedicated peering path or an L4 proxy in front of the appliance.
